endorsements.quote: Any AI-generated content that contributes to manuscripts or interpretations should be disclosed, in line with ethical publishing standards.
Researchers must therefore approach GenAI chatbot-generated content with caution and always verify outputs through manual searching and consultation with librarians or methodological experts.

unlisted_practices: Treat AI-generated content as a draft or starting point that must be critically evaluated and verified against credible sources before use.
Design prompts with clear context, structure, and iterative refinement to improve output relevance and accuracy.
Construct prompts that emphasize cultural sensitivity, accuracy, and nuance in traditional, complementary, and integrative medicine research.
Do not upload sensitive or identifiable data to third-party generative AI platforms without confirming compliance with confidentiality, consent, privacy law, and IRB requirements.
Do not credit generative AI chatbots as authors; researchers remain accountable for AI-assisted work.
Educate researchers about prompt engineering to support effective and responsible use of generative AI chatbots.
Review and test AI-generated statistical code line by line on actual datasets and validate against authoritative sources before use.
Evaluate AI-generated implementation strategies through stakeholder consultation and expert input.

screen.reason: Practical guide and recommendations for TCIM researchers on prompt engineering and responsible use of GenAI chatbots; not an empirical study.
